concerns.text: The plan relies on a synthetic placeholder image set because Visual Genome is not a verified source. This threatens external validity: causal claims about visual salience on moral judgments may not generalize to real-world images, yet the specification presents the inference as broadly applicable.

While a Latin‑Square schedule is used, the plan does not describe any wash‑out period, breaks, or checks for fatigue/learning effects across the within‑subject blocks. Residual carry‑over could confound the salience manipulation, weakening causal attribution.

If the primary CLMM fails, the fallback is a Linear Mixed Model (LMM) on ordinal data or Wilcoxon tests. Applying an LMM to a 1‑7 Likert outcome violates the ordinal nature of the response and may produce biased estimates, compromising the validity of any conclusions drawn from the fallback analysis.

The a‑priori power analysis assumes a medium effect (odds ratio ≈ 1.5) without citing empirical priors or meta‑analytic evidence. If the true effect is smaller, the planned N≈600 could be insufficient, risking under‑power and unreliable inference.

The exclusion rule flags participants with variance < 0.1 OR > 90 % identical ratings, but does not incorporate attention‑check failures or response time checks. Relying solely on variance may miss inattentive participants, introducing noise that can attenuate the estimated salience effect.
